rv.q: The playwright Eliya Smith’s strange, unexpectedly tender theatrical investigation draws on interviews with eight men to unpack the legacy of the infamous viral phenomenon 2 Girls 1 Cup...
That sort of mental contagion is actually the subject of this strangely chilly show, which eventually becomes a discussion about when a girl’s self-loathing first sets in.
Two Girls confirmed me what’s worth watching: not that notorious video but the career of a playwright on the ascent.
Chloe Claudel and Juliana Sass hilariously perform these interviews verbatim.
That final twist, for me, is more successful intellectually than emotionally.
What an inventive and delightful show this was.
Except the sudden veer into this new idea happens far too late to feel like a fully formed thematic device, let alone the show’s defining message.

cn.t: Critics find this verbatim play about the infamous viral video to be a tricky but intriguing examination of internet porn's impact on millennials, though some question whether Smith's documentary approach fully succeeds.

vr.q: The way the piece reveals itself in how and why it was created is perfectly paced and compelling from start to finish.
